title: Present ignorance and failures of imagination are no premise for a hard problem

statements.text: Setting consciousness apart as the hard problem is unconvincing and counterproductive. Using present ignorance as a premise about what can never be discovered is a fallacy, and so is the "I cannot imagine" argument: when little is known, inability to imagine a mechanism is an uninteresting fact about the speaker, not a metaphysical fact about the world. The task is to see how far a neurobiological approach gets.

sources.quote: Use of our current ignorance as a premise to determine what we can never discover is one common logical flaw.
our inability to imagine a mechanism is a rather uninteresting psychological fact about us, not an interesting metaphysical fact about the world
